Subject: Post-demo recap + POC test matrix: dedicated reserved vs hyperscaler

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion and very helpful context on the production targets. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the POC scope.

Key priorities you called out:
- Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for short interactive prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Sustained throughput: 200 req/s for 2k-token average workloads during business hours.
- Cost target: reduce per-1k-token inference cost compared to your current hyperscaler baseline (target: < $0.20/1k tokens).
- Security/compliance: VPC peering or Private deployment + KMS-managed keys; retention 30 days, audit logs required.

What we propose for an apples-to-apples evaluation:
1) Hyperscaler baseline test: run your current model on their managed endpoints with identical prompt sets and token distributions. We need the exact endpoint configuration (GPU type, instance size, concurrency) you plan to compare.
2) Redwood Dedicated reserved pool: a 2-week trial with reserved GPUs sized to meet the 200 req/s sustained throughput target; we will run the same prompt sets and synthetic concurrency profiles.
3) Degradation & fallback scenarios: simulate regional capacity pressure and validate our fallback to compatible model variants and autoscaling behavior.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Share the representative prompt set and token distribution (short vs long).
- Confirm the hyperscaler instance family you want us to mirror (e.g., A100/Trn1/NVIDIA H100).
- Approve the attached draft POC plan and checklist so we can schedule infra and monitoring.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler_v1.pdf, medatlas-poc-checklist.xlsx

Proposed timeline:
- Confirm test inputs by EOD Wednesday 9/15
- Kickoff week of 9/20 (we'll reserve capacity once checklist is approved)

Next step: can we lock a 30-minute kickoff on either Tue 9/21 or Wed 9/22 to walk the test plan?

Thanks,

Laura Bennett

Adding a technical test checklist so we don't miss the important comparisons. Attaching a short script we use to drive concurrency (test-commands.sh).

Minimum configuration items we should capture from MedAtlas for the hyperscaler baseline:
- Exact GPU SKU and vCPU/memory of the endpoint(s).
- Batch and concurrency config used in their managed endpoint (max_batch_size, preferred_batch_latency_ms).
- Average tokens per request and peak tokens observed during business hours.

Redwood Dedicated test cases (we'll run these):
A) Short prompt latency profile: 1–256 tokens, ramp concurrency 1->200, measure p50/p95/p99 and tail queuing.
B) Long-context throughput: 2k-token average, sustained 200 req/s for 30 minutes.
C) Mixed realistic workload: sampled traffic from your provided set with KV-cache warmed.
D) Failure/fallback: step down capacity to simulate regional outage and validate automatic fallback to variant model with preserved SLA.

Data to capture for all tests:
- Per-token cost estimate, including GPU utilization, batch efficiency, KV cache hit rate.
- End-to-end latency broken out by queueing, token generation, and post-processing.

Let's also agree on measurements: p95 latency and 95th percentile token generation time per step. If MedAtlas can share a short Prometheus export or sample traces that will help correlate.

Karthik
